summary: Blueprint for modular symbols and analytic p-adic L-functions of modular forms. This first checkpoint plans the algebraic core of L0 from Pollack–Stevens, 'Overconvergent modular symbols and p-adic L-functions' (Ann. Sci. ENS 2011), §2.1–2.2 and §3.4: the Steinberg module Δ₀ = Div⁰(P¹(ℚ)) with its GL₂(ℚ)-action, V-valued modular symbols for a finite-index Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ), Manin's unimodular map d : ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] → Δ₀ with its surjectivity (continued fractions) and kernel (the Manin relations 1 + σ, 1 + τ + τ², and 1 − (−1) over SL₂(ℤ)), the coset basis of ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] over ℤ[Γ], the coefficient modules V_k = Sym^k with the adjugate action, the monoid Σ₀(N), the Hecke operators T_ℓ and U_q, and the involution at infinity with the plus/minus decomposition. The cohomological comparison, the explicit Manin presentation, Eichler–Shimura and stages L1–L4 remain.

nodes.title: The Steinberg module Δ₀ = Div⁰(P¹(ℚ))
nodes.statement: Δ₀ ⊆ ℤ[P¹(ℚ)] is the group of degree-zero divisors on P¹(ℚ) = ℚ ∪ {∞}, a left ℤ[GL₂(ℚ)]-module through the action of GL₂(ℚ) on P¹(ℚ) by linear fractional transformations. It is generated by the divisors {b} − {a}.
hypotheses: P¹(ℚ) is Mathlib's OnePoint ℚ with its GL₂(ℚ)-action (OnePoint.instGLAction).
proofSteps: Define Δ₀ as the kernel of the degree map ℤ[P¹(ℚ)] → ℤ (Finsupp.linearCombination with all weights 1).
The permutation action g·{x} = {g x} preserves the degree, hence Δ₀.
Generation: a divisor Σ n_x {x} of degree 0 equals Σ n_x ({x} − {∞}).
acceptance: A single point {∞} is not in Δ₀.
The scalar matrices act trivially, so the action factors through PGL₂(ℚ); in particular −1 ∈ SL₂(ℤ) acts trivially.

uses.how: modular symbols are Γ-equivariant maps out of Δ₀.
evaluation of symbols at {∞} − {0} and {∞} − {a/m} gives twisted L-values.

api.name: TauCeti.ModularSymbol.Delta0
api.statement: Δ₀ as a submodule of ℤ[P¹(ℚ)].

nodes.title: Modular symbols
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) of finite index and a right ℤ[Γ]-module V, Symb_Γ(V) is the group of additive maps φ : Δ₀ → V with φ(γD) = φ(D)|γ^{-1} for all γ ∈ Γ, D ∈ Δ₀. In the formal version V carries the left representation ρ(γ)v = v|γ^{-1}, and the condition reads φ(γD) = ρ(γ)φ(D).
hypotheses: Γ acts on Δ₀ through SL₂(ℤ) → GL₂(ℚ).
Left/right conventions: Pollack–Stevens' right action v|γ is recorded as the left representation v ↦ v|γ^{-1}.
proofSteps: Define symbols Γ ρ as the additive subgroup of maps Δ₀ → V satisfying the equivariance; closure under sums and negatives is immediate.
A modular symbol is determined by its values on the unimodular divisors {γ0} − {γ∞} (manin-surjectivity).
acceptance: Symb_{SL₂(ℤ)}(ℤ) = 0: by the Manin relations φ({0} − {∞}) = v satisfies 2v = 0 and 3v = 0.
Symb_{Γ₀(11)}(ℤ) has rank 3 = 2g + (c − 1), with genus g = 1 and c = 2 cusps.
When the orders of torsion elements act invertibly on V, Symb_Γ(V) ≅ H¹_c(H/Γ, Ṽ) (Pollack–Stevens, citing Ash–Stevens [2, Prop. 4.2]); planned as remaining work.

uses.how: the plus/minus eigensymbols of a newform and its periods.
distribution-valued symbols lifting polynomial-valued ones (control theorem).

sources.match: The definition, with ϕ ∈ SymbΓ(V) ⟺ ϕ(γD) = ϕ(D)|γ⁻¹.

nodes.title: The unimodular map d : ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] → Δ₀
nodes.statement: d is the ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)]-linear map sending γ = (a b; c d) to {γ0} − {γ∞} = {b/d} − {a/c}, the boundary of the unimodular path [γ] from a/c to b/d.
hypotheses: γ acts through SL₂(ℤ) → GL₂(ℚ) on P¹(ℚ).
proofSteps: Define d on the basis γ of ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] by the displayed divisor and extend linearly; equivariance d(gx) = g·d(x) follows from g·({γ0} − {γ∞}) = {gγ0} − {gγ∞}.
acceptance: d(−γ) = d(γ), since −1 acts trivially.

sources.match: The map d (Pollack–Stevens over G = PSL₂(ℤ)).

api.name: TauCeti.ModularSymbol.unimodularMap_of_mul
api.statement: d(g·γ) = g · d(γ): d is SL₂(ℤ)-equivariant.

nodes.title: Every divisor is a sum of unimodular divisors
nodes.statement: d : ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] → Δ₀ is surjective: every degree-zero divisor on P¹(ℚ) is a ℤ-combination of unimodular divisors {γ0} − {γ∞}.
proofSteps: By span_divisorOf it suffices to treat {r} − {∞} for r = a/c ∈ ℚ in lowest terms (and {∞} − {∞} = 0).

Let p_i/q_i be the convergents of the continued fraction of r, with p_{−1}/q_{−1} = 1/0 = ∞. Then {r} − {∞} = Σ_i ({p_i/q_i} − {p_{i−1}/q_{i−1}}), and p_i q_{i−1} − p_{i−1} q_i = ±1, so each term is ±d(γ_i) for γ_i = (p_{i−1} ±p_i; q_{i−1} ±q_i) ∈ SL₂(ℤ).
acceptance: For r = 1/2 the convergents are 0/1 and 1/2, so {1/2} − {∞} = ({0} − {∞}) + ({1/2} − {0}), and both terms are unimodular (0·2 − 1·1 = −1).
Manin's trick; the formal proof can reuse Mathlib's continued fractions (GenContFract) or Euclid's algorithm directly.

nodes.title: The Manin relations
nodes.statement: ker d is the left ideal of ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] generated by 1 + σ, 1 + τ + τ² and 1 − (−1), where σ = (0 −1; 1 0) and τ = (0 −1; 1 −1); hence Δ₀ ≅ ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)]/ker d. Modulo 1 − (−1) this is Manin's presentation Δ₀ ≅ ℤ[PSL₂(ℤ)]/(ℤ[G](1 + τ + τ²) + ℤ[G](1 + σ)).
hypotheses: The generator 1 − (−1) appears because the formalisation works over SL₂(ℤ), in which −1 acts trivially on P¹(ℚ).
proofSteps: The listed elements lie in ker d (unimodular-map).

Farey tessellation: unimodular paths are the edges and the images of the triangle 0, 1, ∞ are the faces of a PSL₂(ℤ)-invariant decomposition of H* with vertex set P¹(ℚ); PSL₂(ℤ) acts simply transitively on oriented edges and with stabiliser ⟨τ⟩ on faces.

Cellular chains relative to the vertices: the 1-chains are ℤ[G]/ℤ[G](1 + σ) (reversing an edge) and the 2-chains ℤ[G/⟨τ⟩], with boundary x ↦ x(1 + τ + τ²). Since H* is contractible, the long exact sequence of the pair identifies H₁(H*, P¹(ℚ)) with Δ₀ through the boundary map, and cellular homology computes it as C₁/∂C₂; hence ker d = ℤ[G](1 + σ) + ℤ[G](1 + τ + τ²).
Pull back along ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] → ℤ[PSL₂(ℤ)], whose kernel is generated by 1 − (−1). Pollack–Stevens cite Manin without proof; an algebraic alternative uses PSL₂(ℤ) ≅ ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/3.
acceptance: For Γ torsion-free, the resulting presentation of Δ₀ as a ℤ[Γ]-module has a single relation (Pollack–Stevens Theorem 2.6, remaining work).
Symb_{SL₂(ℤ)}(ℤ) = 0 follows at once.
The ideal is a left ideal: it is not two-sided.

uses.how: a symbol is determined by a vector v_i per coset satisfying the two- and three-term Manin relations.
the explicit presentation behind the control theorem's difference equation.

nodes.title: ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] is free over ℤ[Γ]
nodes.statement: For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ), ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] is a free left ℤ[Γ]-module, with basis any set of right coset representatives of Γ\SL₂(ℤ).
hypotheses: Γ acts by left multiplication through the inclusion.
proofSteps: SL₂(ℤ) = ⊔_i Γ g_i gives ℤ[SL₂(ℤ)] = ⊕_i ℤ[Γ]g_i, and γ g_i ↦ (γ, i) is a bijection Γ × (Γ\SL₂(ℤ)) → SL₂(ℤ).
acceptance: For finite index the basis is finite, of size [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ].
Combined with the Manin relations this gives the ℤ[Γ]-presentation of Δ₀ by coset generators.

nodes.title: The coefficient modules V_k = Sym^k
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R and k ≥ 0, V_k(R) is the R-module of homogeneous polynomials of degree k in X, Y, with the right action of integral matrices of nonzero determinant (P|γ)(X, Y) = P((X, Y)·γ*) = P(dX − cY, −bX + aY) for γ = (a b; c d), γ* its adjugate; restricted to Γ it gives the left representation γ ↦ (P ↦ P|γ^{-1}).
hypotheses: The adjugate keeps the action integral, so it is defined for the monoid of integral matrices, not only GL₂(ℚ).
proofSteps: V_k(R) := MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) R k; P|γ := aeval of the substitution X ↦ dX − cY, Y ↦ −bX + aY, which preserves degree k.
Right action: (γδ)* = δ*γ* gives P|(γδ) = (P|γ)|δ.
acceptance: rank V_k(R) = k + 1.
A scalar matrix c·1 acts by c^k.
V_0 is the trivial representation; Pollack–Stevens use V_k = Sym^k(ℚ_p²) with the same formula.

uses.how: V_k-valued symbols attached to weight k + 2 forms through Eichler–Shimura.

nodes.title: The monoid Σ₀(N)
nodes.statement: Σ₀(N) is the monoid of integral matrices (a b; c d) with nonzero determinant, N | c and (a, N) = 1; it contains Γ₀(N) and the matrices (ℓ 0; 0 1) for (ℓ, N) = 1 and (1 a; 0 ℓ) for all a, ℓ ≥ 1.
proofSteps: Closure: the lower-left entry of a product is c a′ + d c′ ≡ 0 mod N, and the upper-left entry a a′ + b c′ ≡ a a′ mod N is prime to N; determinants multiply.
acceptance: Γ₀(N) ⊆ Σ₀(N) (Gamma0_le_Sigma0).
(1 a; 0 ℓ) ∈ Σ₀(N) for every a and ℓ ≥ 1; (ℓ 0; 0 1) ∈ Σ₀(N) iff (ℓ, N) = 1.
This is Pollack–Stevens' S₀(p) with p replaced by N.

uses.how: Hecke operators are sums of the Σ₀(N)-slash over coset representatives.

nodes.title: Hecke operators on modular symbols
nodes.statement: For V with a right Σ₀(N)-action extending its Γ₀(N)-action, and φ ∈ Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V): (φ|δ)(D) := φ(δD)|δ; for a prime ℓ ∤ N, φ|T_ℓ := φ|(ℓ 0; 0 1) + Σ_{a=0}^{ℓ−1} φ|(1 a; 0 ℓ); for q | N, φ|U_q := Σ_{a=0}^{q−1} φ|(1 a; 0 q). These preserve Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V) and commute.
hypotheses: V's Γ₀(N)-action is the restriction of the Σ₀(N)-action.
proofSteps: The listed matrices are representatives of Γ₀(N)\Γ₀(N)(ℓ 0; 0 1)Γ₀(N) (resp. for U_q); right multiplication by γ ∈ Γ₀(N) permutes the cosets, so Σ φ|α_i is again Γ₀(N)-invariant.

The operators come from an action of the Γ₀(N) Hecke ring of double cosets on Symb_{Γ₀(N)}(V), with T_ℓ the class of Γ₀(N)(ℓ 0; 0 1)Γ₀(N); commutativity follows from commutativity of that ring (Tau Ceti HeckeRing.GL2.commRingHeckeRingGamma0).
acceptance: On Symb_{Γ₀(11)}(ℤ), T_2 has characteristic polynomial (x − 3)(x + 2)²: eigenvalue 3 on the boundary (Eisenstein) part and a₂(11a) = −2 on the plus and minus parts.
On the same space T_3 has characteristic polynomial (x − 4)(x + 1)².
U_q is defined without the (q 0; 0 1) term.

uses.how: U_p on distribution-valued symbols in the control theorem.

nodes.title: The involution at infinity
nodes.statement: ι = (−1 0; 0 1) acts on P¹(ℚ) by x ↦ −x; when ι normalises Γ (for instance Γ = Γ₀(N)) and V carries a compatible action of ι, φ ↦ φ|ι is an involution of Symb_Γ(V).
hypotheses: ι normalises Γ; V has an action of the monoid generated by Γ and ι.
proofSteps: ι² = 1; ι Γ₀(N) ι^{-1} = Γ₀(N) since conjugation changes the signs of b and c; (φ|ι)|ι = φ.
acceptance: ι · x = −x on P¹(ℚ) and fixes 0 and ∞.
It is not in SL₂(ℤ) (det ι = −1).

nodes.title: The plus/minus decomposition
nodes.statement: If ι normalises Γ and 2 acts invertibly on V, then Symb_Γ(V) = Symb_Γ(V)^+ ⊕ Symb_Γ(V)^− into ±1-eigenspaces of ι, via φ = (φ + φ|ι)/2 + (φ − φ|ι)/2; the decomposition is preserved by the Hecke operators when ι commutes with them.
proofSteps: The idempotents (1 ± ι)/2 are defined since 2 is invertible and ι² = 1.
acceptance: Over ℤ the decomposition fails in general: Symb^+ ⊕ Symb^− has index a power of 2.
Hecke operators T_ℓ commute with ι (ι normalises the double cosets).

remaining: Compactly supported and parabolic cohomology of the modular curve with boundary maps, and the comparison Symb_Γ(V) ≅ H¹_c(H/Γ, Ṽ) when the orders of torsion elements are invertible on V (Ash–Stevens Proposition 4.2, cited by Pollack–Stevens).
Solving the Manin relations: fundamental domains and the presentation of Δ₀ over ℤ[Γ] (Pollack–Stevens §§2.3–2.5, Theorem 2.6), including the three-torsion case.
Diamond operators and nebentypus, and the Γ₁(N) versions of the Hecke operators.

Eichler–Shimura period maps at general level: rational structures, Hecke equivariance, injectivity and eigenspace dimensions; elliptic stabilisers through a torsion-free auxiliary level and descent; comparison with the analytic modular-curve carrier.
coverage.notes: This checkpoint plans the algebraic core of L0 from Pollack–Stevens §2.1–2.2 and §3.4: the Steinberg module, modular symbols, the unimodular map with Manin's surjectivity and relations (over SL₂(ℤ), with −1 as an extra relation), the coset basis, the coefficient modules V_k, the monoid Σ₀(N), Hecke operators and the involution at infinity with the plus/minus decomposition. AUDIT-26 records L0 as not built; the only library inputs are Mathlib's P¹, GL₂ action, congruence subgroups and polynomial modules, and Tau Ceti's Γ₀(N) Hecke ring.
